results.prompt: Make a mono green storm deck in Premodern.
results.text:
This is a brew. It is legal in Premodern, but no mono green storm deck has shown up in results.

**The storm card.** Green has one legal storm card in Premodern: Hunting Pack. It costs 7 and makes a 4/4 Beast for each copy, so the deck is built around it. It shows up in 31 decks in the format. The Elves deck is the only close shell, and it plays it in 1 of 7 lists (2 copies). The other storm cards are off color or illegal here:
- Brain Freeze is blue and Dragonstorm is red.
- Tendrils of Agony, Mind's Desire, Grapeshot and Empty the Warrens are illegal.

**How it plays.** You make a lot of mana and cast several cheap spells in one turn. Then you cast Hunting Pack with storm.
- **Mana creatures (15):** 4 Llanowar Elves, 4 Fyndhorn Elves, 4 Birds of Paradise, 3 Wall of Roots. The Elves list runs the same elves at 3.4 copies each.
- **Quirion Ranger (3):** Elves runs 3.3 copies. It untaps a mana creature and costs no spell slot.
- **Free spells:** 4 Lotus Petal and 4 Land Grant. Both add to the storm count. Land Grant costs nothing when you hold no lands.
- **Mana enchantments:** 4 Wild Growth (588 decks), 2 Overgrowth and 2 Vernal Bloom. Overgrowth and Vernal Bloom are legal but have not shown up in results.
- **Early Harvest (3):** It untaps your basic lands. It also has not shown up in results. With Wild Growth or Overgrowth on a Forest, one cast nets mana.
- **Sylvan Library (3):** It digs for Hunting Pack. It appears in 4 Elves-adjacent lists at 3.5 copies.
- **Lands (16):** 14 Forest and 2 Gaea's Cradle. Early Harvest and Land Grant want basic Forests, so Cradle stays at 2.

**Sideboard.** The Elves sideboard shows Naturalize in all 7 decks, so I kept 3. That also covers Enchantress. The rest are mostly from that list:
- 2 Tormod's Crypt
- 2 Wall of Blossoms
- 3 Xantid Swarm
- 1 Uktabi Orangutan
- 1 Nantuko Vigilante
- 2 Yavimaya Elder
- 1 Scroll Rack

**Weak points.** You have no removal and no counter-magic, and almost every spell is a mana source with no impact on the board. A Hunting Pack with storm 4 or more is the only way you win quickly. Stiflenought, Sligh and Terrageddon will pressure you before you get there. If you want a more proven build, I can adapt the Elves list instead. It runs Anger, Deranged Hermit and Survival of the Fittest, and it is no longer mono green.

results.prompt: Build a Replenish deck in Premodern that doesn't play blue.
results.text:
I built a green-white Replenish list with no blue cards. It is a brew, not a stock list.

**Why it is a brew**
- The 37 Replenish lists in the results are all blue-white. Island, Adarkar Wastes, Skycloud Expanse, Decree of Silence, Frantic Search, Intuition and Mana Leak all need blue.
- Attunement also needs blue ({2}{U}). I first put it in, then took it out.
- Only 2 of the 37 Replenish lists play any green. Wild Mongrel is not in the Replenish results.
- The closest real shell is Enchantress, with 96 decks in the results. Its winning list (walrusmadness, 8-0, Challenge 16) already runs 2 Replenish. I used that shell and raised Replenish to 4.
- Wild Mongrel appears in 196 recent lists in the format. It has not shown up in any Enchantress or Replenish list.

**How it works**
- **Replenish (4):** the Replenish lists run it at 100%, averaging 3.9 copies.
- **Getting enchantments into the graveyard:**
  - Wild Mongrel (4) discards any card. It also replaces Attunement as a creature.
  - Seal of Cleansing (3, 100% in both archetypes) sacrifices itself.
  - Sterling Grove (3) sacrifices itself to fetch an enchantment.
- **Opalescence (3) and Parallax Wave (3):** both are stock in Replenish and Enchantress. Replenish into Opalescence makes your enchantments into creatures.
- **Argothian Enchantress (4) and Enchantress's Presence (4):** both are 100% stock in Enchantress. They draw cards off every enchantment.
- **Mana:** Wild Growth (3), 4 Brushland, 4 Windswept Heath, 2 Wooded Foothills and 4 Serra's Sanctum, plus 5 Forest and 3 Plains. That is 22 lands. Serra's Sanctum is 100% stock in Enchantress.
- **Other cards:** Swords to Plowshares (3), Mirri's Guile (2), Solitary Confinement (1) and Abeyance (1).

**Sideboard (15)**
- This is the Enchantress board: 2 Aura of Silence, 1 Karmic Justice, 2 Sacred Ground, 1 Sphere of Law, 2 Tormod's Crypt, 2 Warmth, 3 Xantid Swarm and 1 Swords to Plowshares.
- I added 1 Exalted Angel. It is a non-blue card from the Replenish sideboard (97% of Replenish lists run it).
- I did not use the usual Replenish sideboard otherwise. Meddling Mage and Hydroblast are blue, and Defense Grid is not a card I chose.

**Weak points**
- You lose Intuition and Frantic Search, so you have no tutor for Replenish.
- Mongrel is a creature, so it dies to removal before it can discard.
- Mirri's Guile is down to 2 from the Enchantress stock of 4, to make room for Mongrel.

I can build a sideboard for a specific matchup if you name one.

results.prompt: Build a Modern deck around Thassa's Oracle and Tainted Pact.
results.text:
I could not build this around Tainted Pact. Tainted Pact is not legal in Modern, so it can't go in any list. The deck below is a brew with Thassa's Oracle and Spoils of the Vault, which is the closest legal stand-in.

**The brew: Modern UB Oracle (brew, no results behind it)**

- **Thassa's Oracle:** 4 copies. It appears in 22 recent decks. None of those decks were on the Mono-Blue Belcher, Neoform, Frog, Blink, Grixis Control or UW Control lists I checked, so I could not find an existing shell to copy.
- **Spoils of the Vault:** 3 copies. It appears in 150 decks. It fetches a named card and costs 1 life for each card it exiles. In a 60-card deck that is a lot of life, so it is a real risk and not a reliable combo piece.
- **Jace, Wielder of Mysteries:** 2 copies. It appears in 42 decks. It costs {1}{U}{U}{U}, so it adds 3 to your devotion to blue. Its draw-from-an-empty-library win is a second way to win.
- **Interaction and cantrips:** 4 Counterspell, 3 Spell Snare, 2 Force of Negation, 3 Fatal Push, 2 Sheoldred's Edict, 3 Thoughtseize, 4 Preordain and 4 Opt. Fatal Push appears in 19 decks. Thoughtseize appears in 10. Opt has not shown up in recent Modern results.
- **Creatures:** 4 Quantum Riddler and 2 Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student. These give the deck a way to win without the combo.
- **Mana:** 20 lands. They are 4 Watery Grave, 4 Polluted Delta, 4 Undercity Sewers, 5 Island, 1 Swamp, 1 Gloomlake Verge and 1 Darkslick Shores.
- **Sideboard:** 3 Consign to Memory, 2 Sink into Stupor, 2 Drown in the Loch, 1 Sheoldred's Edict, 1 Force of Negation and 1 Thoughtseize. This is a generic board, not built for a specific matchup.

**Weaknesses**
- Oracle only wins if your library is no larger than your devotion to blue. Without Tainted Pact or Demonic Consultation (also illegal), Spoils is the only way to shrink it, and it is slow and costly.
- In most games this plays as a blue-black tempo deck, and Oracle is a 2-mana body that digs a little.

If you want a deck with results behind it, I can build a real list from one of the established strategies instead.

results.prompt: Make a fun mono white control deck for Modern leagues.
results.text:
This is a brew. No mono white control deck shows up in the Modern field. The list is a 60-card main with a 9-card board, and it passed validation.

**The plan:** Trade one-for-one with removal, sweep the board, then win with planeswalkers and angels. The field is fast (Broodscale Combo 17.3%, Prowess 9.3%), so the early game is cheap removal and blockers.

**Cards with results:**
- Solitude: 9 recent decks, usually 4 copies. It's removal that doubles as a free spell when you're behind.
- Ephemerate: 8 decks, about 3 copies. It re-uses Solitude, Skyclave Apparition, Fiend Hunter and Wall of Omens.
- Path to Exile: 1 deck, 4 copies.
- Castle Ardenvale: 1 deck, 2 copies. It makes a 1/1 each turn in a long game.
- Field of Ruin: 2 decks. Two copies can remove nonbasic lands such as Amulet Titan's and Domain Zoo's.
- Skyclave Apparition: 1 deck, 2 copies.
- Wrath of God: 434 decks across the format. Elesh Norn: 338. Wall of Omens: 2.

**Cards with no results (brew picks):** Oblivion Ring, Fiend Hunter, Sunfall, Lone Missionary, Restoration Angel, Archangel Avacyn, Gideon Jura, Elspeth, Sun's Champion, Baneslayer Angel.

**Not in the list:** The tool flags Swords to Plowshares, Council's Judgment, Armageddon, Unexpectedly Absent and Palace Jailer as not legal here, so I left them out. I also skipped Prismatic Ending. With only white mana, it can only hit mana value 1 or less.

**Main deck:**
- **Lands (24):** 17 Plains, 3 Castle Ardenvale, 2 Eiganjo, 2 Field of Ruin.
- **Cheap interaction:** 4 Path to Exile, 3 Oblivion Ring, 2 Ephemerate.
- **Early plays:** 3 Wall of Omens, 2 Lone Missionary (gains 4 life against aggro).
- **Creature removal:** 3 Skyclave Apparition, 2 Fiend Hunter, 4 Solitude.
- **Sweepers:** 3 Wrath of God, 1 Sunfall.
- **Win conditions:** 2 Restoration Angel, 2 Archangel Avacyn, 2 Gideon Jura, 2 Elspeth, Sun's Champion, 1 Elesh Norn.

**Sideboard:**
- 3 Mana Tithe for Storm and combo decks.
- 2 Day of Judgment and 1 Sunfall (the second copy) for more sweepers.
- 2 Timely Reinforcements for aggro decks.
- 1 Baneslayer Angel.

**Weak spots:** The top end is heavy. There are 13 cards that cost 5 or more. Field of Ruin makes WW costs harder to cast. The deck has no card draw beyond Wall of Omens. Test it in a League before you commit.

I built a 15-card sideboard for your main deck, and the server accepted it as a legal Legacy list. I left your 60 untouched. The sideboard follows the 141 Dimir Tempo sideboards in the current window, adjusted for the top matchups.

**Sideboard**
- 2 Consign to Memory. It's in 100% of Dimir sideboards, at 2.6 copies on average. It counters colorless spells and triggered abilities. Eldrazi Aggro (6.2% of the meta) and Tron (7.2%) play colorless threats. Ocelot Aggro (9.1%) runs 4 Guide of Souls and 4 Ocelot Pride, and both have triggers.
- 2 Force of Negation. It's in 94% of lists, at 1.7 copies. It counters noncreature spells for free on the opponent's turn. Doomsday (5.7%) and Tron are the main targets.
- 2 Massacre. It's in 80% of lists, at 1.6 copies. Ocelot Aggro plays Plains (94% adoption), so you can cast it for free with your Swamp. The Ocelot deck's Guide of Souls (1/2), Ocelot Pride (1/1), Ajani (1/2) and Amped Raptor (2/1) all die to it. Izzet Tempo's Dragon's Rage Channeler (1/1) and Delver also die to it. Against Eldrazi Aggro it costs full price. It kills Glaring Fleshraker and Wastescape Battlemage (both 2/2), but not the 3/3 and larger creatures.
- 2 Nihil Spellbomb. It's in 76% of lists, at 1.8 copies. It's for Reanimator (3.9%), Hogaak (2.2%) and Dredge (1.1%).
- 2 Barrowgoyf. It's in 69% of lists, at 1.9 copies. Deathtouch blocks Reality Smasher (5/5) and Thought-Knot Seer (4/4). Lifelink helps against Ocelot Aggro.
- 2 Hydroblast. It's in 65% of lists, at 1.6 copies. It hits red cards: Dragon's Rage Channeler (98% in Izzet Tempo) and Amped Raptor (99% in Ocelot Aggro). It also hits Phlage (39% in Ocelot Aggro).
- 2 Snuff Out. It's in 31% of sideboards as a flex card, and 61% of main decks. It's a free removal spell against nonblack creatures. Ocelot Aggro and Eldrazi Aggro play only nonblack creatures.
- 1 Bloodchief's Thirst. It's in 28% of lists, at 1.4 copies. Unkicked, it kills Ajani, Ocelot Pride and Dragon's Rage Channeler. Kicked, it kills any creature, such as Thought-Knot Seer.

**Cards I left out**
- Null Rod (33% of lists). None of the previews showed artifacts that would justify it. Add it back only if you expect Affinity (1.2% of the meta).
- Toxic Deluge (26%). Massacre and Snuff Out already cover the small creatures. Deluge would cost too much life against Eldrazi's large creatures.
- Surgical Extraction (9%) and Damping Sphere (8%). Both are fringe, and nothing in the previews called for them.

The sideboard scoring tool returned "hit" for every card I tested, so it didn't narrow the choices. I picked cards from the matchup previews and the adoption numbers.

I also didn't check your main against the field. Your main plays 4 Thoughtseize and 4 Fatal Push, and stock lists average 3.6 and 3.3 of them. It has no Nethergoyf, Moonshadow or Mishra's Bauble, which are in 76%, 72% and 69% of main decks. Your Tamiyo count (4) is high next to the 30% adoption, so this main is closer to a brew than a stock list.

results.prompt: Build a Pioneer deck around Greasefang, Okiba Boss that isn't the usual list.
results.text:
I built an Abzan (white, black, green) Greasefang list. It's a brew: no single list in the results plays this exact mix. Greasefang, Okiba Boss is legal and appears in 37 Greasefang decks as a 4-of.

**The idea.** The usual WB list (37 decks) leans on Monument to Endurance, Iron-Shield Elf and The Mycosynth Gardens. I cut those for the green flex cards that showed up in 7 of the 37 decks.

- **Esika's Chariot (3 copies, 7 decks).** Greasefang returns it with haste. It attacks and makes two Cats, and the attack trigger copies a token. It can crew itself from the Cats.
- **Formidable Speaker (4 copies, 7 decks).** Discard Parhelion II and fetch Greasefang. This is the extra tutor the stock list lacks.
- **Yathan Roadwatcher (2 copies, 7 decks).** It mills four and returns a creature with mana value 3 or less. That can be Greasefang or Speaker. It is the only card here that needs all three colors.
- **Cache Grab (3 copies, 7 decks).** It mills four and can take a permanent. That puts a Parhelion II in the graveyard.
- **Thundering Broodwagon (2 copies, 7 decks).** When it enters, it destroys a nonland permanent with mana value 4 or less. It also cycles for {2} if you draw it early.
- **Overlord of the Balemurk (1 copy, 7 decks).** It mills four and returns a creature.

**Kept from stock.** Parhelion II (4 copies, 37 decks), Thoughtseize, Fatal Push, Vanishing Verse (2 copies, 26 decks), Fleeting Spirit and Guardian of New Benalia. These are your discard outlets, and the first two are also your early plays.

**Mana.** The 24 lands are mostly duals: Temple Garden, Blooming Marsh, Godless Shrine, Concealed Courtyard, Overgrown Tomb, Pathway and Multiversal Passage.
- **Overgrown Tomb:** only 3 of the 37 decks play it.
- **Forest:** 4 of 37 decks.
- **Risk:** three colors and a thin land count make this less consistent than stock.

**Sideboard.** It is the field's usual Greasefang board: Soul-Guide Lantern, Bitter Triumph, Duress, Pest Control, Doorkeeper Thrull, Vanishing Verse, Loran of the Third Path and Ral Zarek, Guest Lecturer. I didn't tailor it to a matchup. Tell me which deck you expect and I'll rework it.

results.prompt: Make a Vintage artifact aggro deck.
results.text:
Raker Shops is the artifact aggro deck here.I built Raker Shops, the artifact aggro deck in the current Vintage field. It has 8.5% meta share, 40 appearances and tier B. The server accepted the list as a stock build.

The main deck is the 8-1 list from zippzipp_ at Vintage Challenge 32. It matches the stock core across 61 decks.

**Threats and engines**
- Glaring Fleshraker ×4 (100% of decks) and Scrawling Crawler ×4 (87%).
- Tezzeret, Cruel Captain ×4 (98%), The One Ring ×4 (97%) and Karn, the Great Creator ×1 (100%).
- The Fantasticar ×1 (93%).

**Mana and artifacts**
- The full Mox set and Black Lotus (98%), Mana Crypt, Mana Vault, Sol Ring and Grim Monolith ×4.
- Mox Opal ×2 (57%). The reference list plays 2, and the field averages 1.8.

**Lands**
- Mishra's Workshop ×4 and Ancient Tomb ×4.
- Talon Gates of Madara ×3 (97%).
- One each of City of Traitors (85%), Inventors' Fair (77%), Tolarian Academy and Urza's Saga.

**Utility**
- Sensei's Divining Top ×4 and Manifold Key ×3.
- Chalice of the Void (97%), Pithing Needle (85%), Mystic Forge, Time Vault and Vexing Bauble.

**Sideboard**
It is the field's average board: Defense Grid ×3, Mindbreak Trap ×3, Argentum Masticore ×2, Dismember ×2, Grafdigger's Cage ×2, Portable Hole ×2 and Mycosynth Lattice ×1.

Lodestone Golem (43%) and Trinisphere (43%) are flex slots. They are not in this list. Tell me if you want one swapped in. I can also tune the sideboard for a named matchup.

results.prompt: Give me a strong Golgari midrange list for Standard.
results.text:
This is a Golgari midrange list for Standard with 25 lands and a planeswalker and removal core.

**The data is thin.** Golgari Midrange has only 4 decks in the 30-day window, and it isn't on the tier list. The results are:
- 1-3 at Challenge 16
- 0-2 at Challenge 16
- one 5-0 League list, which was a Warg tribal build
- one Challenge 16 list at place 17 with no record

So I can't call any of it proven. The list is built from the cards the four decks share.

**Core, from the 4 decks:**
- Professor Dellian Fel: 4 of 4 decks, 4 copies here.
- Requiting Hex: 4 of 4 decks, 4 copies.
- Bitter Triumph: 3 of 4 decks, 3 copies.
- Maelstrom Pulse: 3 of 4 decks, 2 copies.
- Shoot the Sheriff: 3 of 4 decks. It's at 1 copy here, which is under the 2.3 average.
- Vraska, the Cutting Glare: 2 of 4 decks, 3 copies.
- Garruk, Veiled Butcher: 2 of 4 decks, 3 copies.
- Emeritus of Abundance: 2 of 4 decks, 3 copies.
- Duress: 2 of 4 decks. I cut it to 2 main, below the 3 average, and moved 2 more to the board.
- Lands: Wastewood Verge, Overgrown Tomb and Deathcap Glade appear in all 4 decks. Restless Cottage is in 3.

**Changes from the 0-2 list I started from:**
- **Tarmogoyf is out.** It is not legal in Standard, even though one list ran 4. I replaced it with 4 Preacher of the Schism. It showed up in one Golgari deck, and it's in 178 decks across the format.
- **Trimmed:** Extrapolate the Impossible, 1 Duress and 1 Strategic Betrayal.
- **Added:** 2 Maelstrom Pulse and 1 Shoot the Sheriff. They are in 3 of 4 decks.
- **Kept as one-ofs:** Raven Eagle at 2, Nowhere to Run and Virtue of Persistence. Each showed up in only one list.

**Main (60):**
- **Creatures and walkers:** 3 Emeritus of Abundance, 2 Raven Eagle, 4 Preacher of the Schism, 3 Vraska, the Cutting Glare, 3 Garruk, Veiled Butcher, 4 Professor Dellian Fel
- **Removal and disruption:** 1 Nowhere to Run, 1 Virtue of Persistence, 3 Bitter Triumph, 4 Requiting Hex, 1 Shoot the Sheriff, 2 Maelstrom Pulse, 2 Day of Black Sun, 2 Duress
- **Lands:** 4 Deathcap Glade, 4 Forest, 4 Overgrown Tomb, 4 Restless Cottage, 3 Swamp, 2 Underground Mortuary, 4 Wastewood Verge

**Sideboard (15):**
- 2 Duress
- 3 Strategic Betrayal
- 2 Vicious Rivalry
- 1 Day of Black Sun
- 2 Leatherhead, Swamp Stalker
- 2 Heritage Reclamation
- 2 Intimidation Tactics
- 1 Deadly Cover-up

The sideboard follows the field's usual Golgari board. Duress is in 4 of 4 and Strategic Betrayal in 3 of 4. I didn't tune it for a specific matchup.

**Weak spots:** The deck is light on early creatures. It leans on removal and four-mana planeswalkers.

The strongest data in this lane is the Jund Sacrifice deck, which has 115 appearances and an 11.9% meta share. It's the black-green-red shell with 3 red cards, so it isn't Golgari. If you want results over a pure Golgari build, ask for that list.

results.prompt: Make a Legacy deck that wins on turn 1 every game.
results.text:
No Legacy deck wins on turn 1 every game, and I can't build one. Hands vary, opponents hold counterspells and discard, and a combo deck can't force a perfect draw. This is the closest I found: Sneak and Show, a tier A deck with 3.7% meta share across 28 appearances.

The list is the 8-1 Legacy Challenge 32 first-place list from JPA93 (2026-10-06). The numbers below come from the 35-deck sample.

**How it can win on turn 1**
- Ancient Tomb is in all 35 decks, and City of Traitors is in 34. Lotus Petal is in 34 decks at 4 copies. Together they give you the mana for a turn 1 Show and Tell or Sneak Attack.
- Show and Tell is at 100% (4 copies). Sneak Attack is at 94% (about 3.9 copies).
- The big threats are Emrakul, the Aeons Torn (100%, 3 copies) and Atraxa, Grand Unifier (97%, 4 copies). I also run 1 Griselbrand, which 34% of decks play.
- Simian Spirit Guide (2 copies, 46% adoption) adds extra mana.

**How it protects the turn**
- Force of Will is at 100% (4 copies). Daze (2 copies) is a flex card at 43%. Flusterstorm (2 copies) is at 86%.
- Brainstorm (100%) and Ponder (97%) dig for the combo pieces. Stock Up (100%, 3 copies) refills your hand.

**Sideboard**
- I used the 15 cards from that same winning list.
- It has Hexing Squelcher (3), Consign to Memory (2), and Pyroblast (2).
- It also has Abrade, Brotherhood's End, Faerie Macabre, Grafdigger's Cage, Magus of the Moon, and Mindbreak Trap.
- Hullbreacher and Omniscience are in the board as well.

You will still win on turn 2 or 3 in many games. Some games you will lose to a removal spell, a counterspell, or a hand with no combo pieces. If you want a different fast deck, such as Reanimator or OmniTell, I can build it.

I made three small changes to your UB Psychatog list. Your 60 matches the Premodern Challenge 16 list (the 4-3 and 4-2 finishes), and it is already close to stock. The server validated the new list as legal.

**Main deck (1 swap)**
- **Out:** 1 Thwart. It is in 3 of 37 UB Psychatog decks (8%).
- **In:** 1 Mana Leak. It is in 18 of 37 decks (49%), at 1.4 copies on average.

**Sideboard (3 swaps)**
- **Out:** Morphling and 1 Blue Elemental Blast. Morphling is in 4 of 37 boards (11%). Blue Elemental Blast is in 12 of 37 (32%), at 1.7 copies.
- **Out:** the second Chain of Vapor. It is in 4 of 37 boards (11%). Chain of Vapor is still in the main deck.
- **In:** 2 Tsabo's Web. It is in 34 of 37 boards (92%), at 1.6 copies. The Web draws a card. It also stops lands with non-mana abilities from untapping:
  - Mishra's Factory in Sligh (2.2 expected).
  - Treetop Village (2) and Rishadan Port (1.8) in Terrageddon.
  - Fetchlands in Enchantress. This is a minor effect there.
- **In:** 1 Powder Keg, for 2 total in the 75. It is in 27 of 37 boards (73%), at 1.6 copies. Sligh plays Mogg Fanatic and Grim Lavamancer, and Terrageddon plays Weathered Wayfarer, Nimble Mongoose and Werebear. Stiflenought's Phyrexian Dreadnought has mana value 6, so the Keg only gets it late.

**Current field (30 days)**
- Enchantress 13.8%
- Stiflenought 13.1%
- Sligh 10.6%
- Terrageddon 8.9%

**What the sideboard does against each deck**
- **Enchantress and Terrageddon:**
  - Back to Basics. Enchantress plays 13.8 nonbasic lands. Terrageddon plays 21.7.
  - Annul.
  - Engineered Plague. It works against Argothian Enchantress (0/1 Human Druid) and Terrageddon's Wayfarer and Werebear (Humans).
- **Sligh:** Hydroblast, Blue Elemental Blast, Powder Keg and Engineered Plague. The Plague hits Mogg Fanatic and Grim Lavamancer.
- **Stiflenought:** Annul, Control Magic and Powder Keg for the Dreadnought. Stiflenought runs 16.2 basic lands and 1 nonbasic, so Back to Basics is a miss there. The server scorer flagged it.

**What I left alone**
- The mana base is unchanged: 21 lands, 9 of them black sources.
- Opt is in 20 of 37 decks (54%) at 3.7 copies, but your list runs Impulse and Portent instead. I did not touch that.
- The scorer counted Hydroblast and Blue Elemental Blast as hits against Enchantress. Enchantress has no red cards, so I treat them as Sligh and Goblins cards only. That is why I cut Blue Elemental Blast to 1 and kept Hydroblast at 2.

results.prompt: Combine Living End and Scam into one Modern deck.
results.text:
I couldn't build a real Scam and Living End deck. This list is a Living End deck with a small Scam-style black splash, so treat it as a brew.

**Why Scam doesn't fit**
- `list_strategies` has no Scam entry, and `strategy_card_stats` for Scam returned 0 decks.
- Grief and Fury, the core of Scam, are marked illegal in Modern by `card_lookup`. I couldn't include them.
- Cheap Scam cards like Thoughtseize, Ragavan, Dauthi Voidwalker and Undying Evil also don't work. Living End's cascade spells stop at the first nonland card that costs less than the spell. Any card that costs 1 or 2 turns a cascade into a miss.

**What I built**
- **Base:** the 5-0 Modern League list from Mighty_Ravendark (Oct 13). It's the Temur Living End shell that most of the 80 tracked decks use.
- **Stock cards kept:** 4 Endurance, 4 Subtlety, 4 Wistfulness and 4 Force of Negation are in 100% of the 80 lists. 4 Shardless Agent is in 99%, and 4 Violent Outburst in 85%.
- **Cycling creatures:** 4 Street Wraith (85%) are the cyclers that fill the graveyard. 3 Generous Ent (100%) and 3 Oliphaunt (86%) are big creatures that come back with Living End.
- **Scam link:** I added 2 Demonic Dread, which is black and red cascade. It has not shown up in results. It costs 3, so it only cascades into Living End, which costs 0.
- **Black sources:** I added Watery Grave (14%) and Underground Mortuary (14%) to cast Demonic Dread. They replaced Island and Otawara, Soaring City.
- **Cuts for the two Demonic Dread:** Brazen Borrower and Valakut Awakening.
- **Evoke link:** Subtlety, Endurance and Vibrance are the evoke elementals in this list. They work like the evoke package in Scam, because a creature you evoke goes to the graveyard and Living End brings it back.
- **Sideboard:** Ravendark's own board. It has 4 Mystical Dispute (100% adoption), 2 Brotherhood's End and 2 Faerie Macabre.

**Risks**
- Adding black to the mana is a real cost, and I haven't tested it. If it feels clunky, swap the 2 Demonic Dread for Violent Outburst and the 5-0 list is back.
- Demonic Dread has no results behind it, so I can't cite any numbers for it.

results.prompt: Build a Pauper deck around Kiln Fiend.
results.text:
This is a brew. It is a UR spells deck built around Kiln Fiend (Izzet).

**Where the shell comes from**
- Kiln Fiend is in 26 decks in the format, but none of the strategies I checked run it. I checked Ruby Storm, Mono-Red Rally, Synthesizer, Wildfire, Ponza, Grixis Control, Jeskai Control, Mono-Red and Rogue. The server tagged the list as Rogue with a "brew" badge and confidence 0.
- I borrowed the UR frame from Grixis Control (18 decks). That list runs 4 Volatile Fjord, 4 Brainstorm, 3.8 Ponder, 3.9 Tolarian Terror and 2.8 Spell Pierce. One 5-0 list also ran 3 Guttersnipe.
- Kiln Fiend and Guttersnipe do not appear together in any list I saw. The list is untested.

**Main (60)**
- **Threats, 13:** 4 Kiln Fiend, 3 Guttersnipe, 4 Tolarian Terror, 2 Murmuring Mystic. Terror gets cheaper with every instant or sorcery. Guttersnipe adds reach.
- **Burn, 11:** 4 Lightning Bolt, 3 Chain Lightning, 3 Galvanic Blast, 1 Fireblast. Each one is a trigger for Kiln Fiend and Guttersnipe. Fireblast is a finisher: sacrifice two Mountains for 4 damage and a +3/+0 pump.
- **Cantrips and free spells, 16:** 4 Brainstorm, 3 Ponder, 3 Preordain, 2 Manamorphose, 2 Reckless Impulse, 2 Mutagenic Growth. Manamorphose and Mutagenic Growth cost almost nothing and still pump Kiln Fiend. Mutagenic Growth has appeared in 109 decks.
- **Interaction, 3:** 3 Spell Pierce.
- **Lands, 17:** 4 Volatile Fjord, 7 Mountain, 6 Island.

Gitaxian Probe would fit this deck, but the lookup shows it is illegal in Pauper, so I left it out.

**Sideboard (15)**
This is the Grixis Control board from the tools, trimmed to fit. Annul and Hydroblast showed up in 100% and 83% of those boards, and Pyroblast in 89%. It is a general board, not a plan for one matchup.
- 3 Pyroblast
- 3 Hydroblast
- 3 Annul
- 2 Cast into the Fire
- 2 Vandalblast
- 2 Campfire

**Risks**
- Kiln Fiend is a 1/2 for two mana. It needs a spell in hand to attack well.
- Only 7 Mountains and 4 Fjords for red. Fireblast wants Mountains, so it is a one-of.

Name a matchup and I can tune the board against it.

results.prompt: Build me a Premodern Dream Halls deck that doesn't win with storm.
results.text:
This is a brew. The server passed it as a legal 60 with a 15-card sideboard. It is based on the Dream Halls lists from Premodern Challenges 16 and 32.

**How it wins:** Dream Halls lets you discard a blue card to cast a blue creature for free. Show and Tell and Intuition find the creatures. Morphling is the main win condition, with Mahamoti Djinn as backup.

**What I cut:**
- **Brain Freeze:** it is in 100% of the 5 Dream Halls lists in the results, mostly as the storm finisher. It is out of the main deck and the sideboard.
- **Meditate:** all 5 lists run it (avg 4 copies). It skips your next turn, which hurts when you are trying to attack with creatures. I cut it.
- **Sleight of Hand:** I dropped it for the fewer, deeper draw spells.

**Creatures:**
- **Morphling x3:** it is in 84 decks in the format. It has shroud and flying for blue mana, and it untaps.
- **Mahamoti Djinn x2:** it has not shown up in recent Premodern results. It is a 5/6 flyer. Show and Tell and Intuition both find it.

**Kept from the real lists:**
- **Core:** Dream Halls x4, Show and Tell x3, Intuition x3 and Cunning Wish x2.
- **Draw:** Opportunity x3, Frantic Search x2, Opt x4, Rush of Knowledge x2, Flash of Insight and Deep Analysis. These also give you cards to discard to Dream Halls.
- **Protection:** Arcane Denial x3, Circular Logic, Orim's Chant x2 and Counterspell x2. Counterspell is in 1,449 format decks, but none of the 5 Dream Halls lists play it. Force of Will and Mana Drain are not legal in Premodern.
- **Mana:** Lotus Petal x4, Ancient Tomb x3, City of Traitors, Adarkar Wastes x4, Flooded Strand x4, Svyelunite Temple x2, Island x3 and one Plains for Orim's Chant.

**Sideboard:** This is close to the field's usual board, minus Brain Freeze. It has Chain of Vapor x2, Blue Elemental Blast x2, Hydroblast, Defense Grid x3, Teferi's Response x2, Stifle, Rushing River, Abeyance, Tolarian Winds and Annul. Cunning Wish can fetch any of the instants.

**Risks:** The creatures have no haste, so you give the opponent a turn to answer. Without storm, this is slower than the stock lists. The recent Dream Halls results were 2-3, 2-3 and 3-3, so the stock lists are not dominant either.

results.prompt: Build a deck that best utilizes Peter Parker's Camera.
results.text:
I built an Esper Blink deck with 2 Peter Parker's Camera. The server accepted it as a legal 60 plus a 15-card sideboard. I called propose_deck twice by mistake. Both submissions are identical, so the list above is the final one.

The Camera has not shown up in any recent Modern results, so this is a brew. It is legal in Modern.

The Camera pays {2}, taps, and removes one of its three film counters. Each use copies an activated or triggered ability you control. The deck has many enter and attack triggers to copy:

- **Solitude** copies its exile trigger to remove a second creature.
- **Phelia** copies its attack trigger to flicker a second permanent.
- **Quantum Riddler** copies its draw trigger.
- **Overlord of the Balemurk** copies its mill and return trigger.
- **Witch Enchanter** copies its artifact and enchantment removal.
- **Flickerwisp** and **Emperor of Bones** also give you triggers to copy.

The base is Omegauo's Modern Challenge 64 winner (9-1, 1st place). I cut 1 Thoughtseize (4 to 3) and 1 Fatal Push (4 to 3) for the Cameras. The sideboard is the same as theirs, and I did not tailor it to any matchup.

I would not play more than 2 Cameras. The card does nothing on its own, and each activation costs {2}.

results.text:
I built Hermit Druid Combo. It's a stock list, not a brew. It's a weird deck that has won in this window.

**Why this deck:** The field lists it as Tier C, with 3.4% meta share across 16 appearances. It also has 26 league trophies, which is a lot for its share.

**How it plays:**
- Hermit Druid (4 copies) mills your library until you hit a basic land. The deck runs no basics, so you mill the whole thing.
- Then you reanimate a payoff. Animate Dead (1 copy) and Shallow Grave (2 copies) do that, and Unearth (3 copies) returns cheap creatures.
- Survival of the Fittest (4 copies) tutors and discards the right creatures.
- Cabal Therapy (4 copies) strips an answer before you go off.
- Krosan Reclamation (1 copy) puts the graveyard back into the library.

**Main deck notes:**
- All the staple cards sit at 88% to 100% adoption in the 42 decks tracked. I changed nothing.
- The list is a 5-0 League list from handle vcT, dated 2026-10-13. I used it as printed.
- The mana is 22 nonbasic lands. They include 4 City of Brass, 4 Gemstone Mine, 4 Llanowar Wastes, 4 Yavimaya Coast and 3 Reflecting Pool.
- 4 Birds of Paradise and 3 Wall of Roots help the mana.

**Sideboard:** It's the field's usual 15 cards. It is not a plan for any one matchup. The main pieces are:
- 2 Duress
- 2 Naturalize
- 2 Pyroclasm
- 2 Xantid Swarm
- 1 Swords to Plowshares

If you tell me which deck you expect to face, I can tune the board for it. Enchantress (13.8%) and Stiflenought (13.1%) are the biggest decks to prepare for.
